answer:
Let \(R,G,B\) denote the numbers of red, green, blue discs drawn, with bounds
\[
0\le R\le4,\qquad 0\le G\le5,\qquad 0\le B\le6.
\]

## 1. Allowing the two pairs to be the same colour

We need two disjoint monochromatic pairs, with no restriction on whether the pairs have the same colour or different colours.

A colour appearing \(c\) times can contribute at most \(\lfloor c/2\rfloor\) disjoint same-colour pairs. So we need
\[
\left\lfloor\frac R2\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac G2\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac B2\right\rfloor \ge 2.
\]

To avoid this, the largest possible draw is
\[
3\text{ red}+1\text{ green}+1\text{ blue},
\]
since \(3\) discs of one colour give only one disjoint pair, and the other colours give none.

Thus:
- \(5\) draws can fail: take \(3R,1G,1B\).
- Any \(6\) draws force two disjoint same-colour pairs.

\[
\boxed{\text{Minimum guaranteed draws }=6.}
\]

Extremal bad draw: \(\boxed{3R+1G+1B}\) with \(5\) discs.

## 2. Requiring the two pairs to have different colours

Now we need two colours each represented at least twice, so that we can take one same-colour pair from each colour.

To avoid this, at most one colour may appear at least twice; every other colour may appear at most once. The largest such draw uses all \(6\) blue discs, plus one red and one green:
\[
6B+1R+1G,
\]
for a total of \(8\) discs. This has only blue pairs available, so it fails the “different colours” requirement.

Therefore:
- \(8\) draws can fail: take \(6B+1R+1G\).
- Any \(9\) draws force two colours each to have at least two discs, giving two disjoint same-colour pairs of different colours.

\[
\boxed{\text{Minimum guaranteed draws }=9.}
\]

Extremal bad draw: \(\boxed{6B+1R+1G}\) with \(8\) discs.

## Final comparison

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Allowing the two pairs to be the same colour: } &&6\text{ draws},\\
&\text{Requiring the two pairs to have different colours: } &&9\text{ draws}.
\end{aligned}}
\]

Extremal bad draws:
\[
\boxed{3R+1G+1B \quad (5\text{ discs})}
\]
for the first case, and
\[
\boxed{6B+1R+1G \quad (8\text{ discs})}
\]
for the second case.
